text.p: Belgian broker Vermeulen Raemdonck maintained its 'buy' rating on stock of oil major PetroFina, saying it expected PetroFina to post a 23 percent rise in 1997 earnings per share and four percent in 1998.

The company clocked up a 61 percent rise in profits in the first six months of the year. Vermeulen Raemdonck said the results of the refining-marketing-transport division would play a crucial role in PetroFina's performance.
Investments in the Fina network in the United States had contributed to the first half and the prospects remained good, it said.

The brokerage said PetroFina, which will list on the New York Stock Exchange next month, would benefit from a reducing tax burden in coming years as highly-taxed Norwegian production is replaced by output from lower-taxed centres such as the United States, Vietnam, Italy and the United Kingdom.
It remained cautious on PetroFina's chemicals operations, but said its focus on monomer production would help offset pressure on polymer prices.
